claims.explanation: GW-583340 is a dual EGFR/ERBB2 inhibitor, so selective killing is most likely driven by dependence on EGFR/ERBB2 signaling. Sensitive lines should have high EGFR or ERBB2 expression, EGFR mutation/amplification, or ERBB2 amplification, while resistance is associated with downstream RAS/RAF pathway activation (KRAS, BRAF, NRAS mutations) or loss of negative regulators like NF1, which bypass the need for upstream EGFR/ERBB2. The pattern of sensitive lines includes known EGFR-mutant/amplified lung and breast lines, and resistant lines are enriched for KRAS/BRAF/NRAS mutations and NF1 loss.

features.basis: Activating EGFR mutations predict response to EGFR inhibitors; HCC4006 is EGFR-mutant and sensitive.
High EGFR expression increases dependence on EGFR signaling; sensitive lines include EGFR-overexpressing breast and lung lines.
ERBB2 (HER2) amplification/overexpression predicts response to dual EGFR/ERBB2 inhibitors; sensitive breast lines include HCC1954 and HDQP1.
KRAS mutations activate downstream MAPK signaling, bypassing EGFR/ERBB2 dependence; resistant lines include NCIH1792, HS766T, PATU8988T.
BRAF mutations drive MAPK pathway independently of EGFR/ERBB2; resistant melanoma and thyroid lines carry BRAF mutations.
NRAS mutations activate downstream signaling and confer resistance to EGFR inhibitors; resistant lines include NCIH1299, KU1919, SW1088.
NF1 loss hyperactivates RAS/MAPK, reducing dependence on upstream EGFR/ERBB2; resistant lines include LOXIMVI, KALS1, UACC62.
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT, providing an EGFR-independent survival signal; resistant lines include UACC62, WM793, KALS1.
PIK3CA mutations can activate PI3K signaling downstream of EGFR; resistant line HGC27 carries PIK3CA mutation.
MET activation can bypass EGFR inhibition; resistant lines 8305C and HGC27 have MET mutations.
ERBB3 mutation may alter heterodimerization and signaling; resistant line NCIH1792 carries ERBB3 mutation.
ARID1A mutations are common in resistant lines and may reflect chromatin remodeling that reduces EGFR dependence; observed in multiple resistant lines.
